decisive_items: Spherical broadly based budding yeast on Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver stain
right-sided ptosis and anisocoria with an asymmetrically miotic right pupil
response.rationale: Blastomycosis is directly supported by positive urine antigen and characteristic broad-based budding yeast on BAL; neurologic signs suggest dissemination. R10 is a broader category, while R1 is the specific etiologic diagnosis.

rejected.why: Histoplasmosis antigen positive but BAL yeast morphology is broad-based budding, typical of Blastomyces, not Histoplasma.
Cryptococcus antigen was negative, and ptosis/anisocoria is not specific to cryptococcosis.
Pneumonia is a generic description; specific fungal evidence points to blastomycosis.
Chronic kidney disease is a comorbidity, not the presenting diagnosis.
No vasculitis or granulomatous features; neurologic findings are explained by disseminated blastomycosis.
No lymphadenopathy or other lymphoma features; cardiac history is incidental.
Cardiovascular disease is a background condition, not the acute illness.
Fungal infection is too broad; blastomycosis is the specific fungal diagnosis.
Disseminated fungal infection is accurate but less specific than blastomycosis; R1 is the precise cause.
